# Codex desktop memory and session-resume report

Observed October 21, 2026 on an Apple silicon M1 MacBook Pro with 8 GiB physical memory.

## Environment

- Desktop app: 26.1016.51333, build 21161, verified after update and restart.
- Bundled backend: codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.11.
- Existing local chats, including image and browser-tool work.

## Symptoms

Previously used chats can remain on Loading model. After updating, an interrupted chat can display a spinning Play control without starting a new backend turn. A fresh ordinary message in that same chat completed successfully in about 40 seconds.

## Confirmed memory observations

The backend process reached approximately 11 GB in macOS top memory accounting, with approximately 10 GB compressed. System memory pressure was critical, swap was about 5.6 GB, and available startup-disk space was 5.5 GiB.

The desktop log recorded that backend exiting with SIGKILL at 16:22:26 UTC and automatically reconnecting to a replacement process. The diagnostic agent did not send that signal. Its sender and exact termination cause are unverified.

After replacement, memory pressure returned to normal, swap fell below 1 GB, and available disk space rose to about 9.5 GiB. The new backend generally measured about 300 to 550 MB during subsequent checks.

A later active browser/tool workload increased the main renderer from under 1 GB to approximately 2.0 to 2.2 GB and returned the system to warning memory pressure. Approximately 2 GB remained attributed to the renderer after the work was saved and paused. This establishes expensive retention during this observation, not an unbounded leak.

## History-size investigation

Two historical transcripts were approximately 11.2 GiB and 8.4 GiB on disk. They were unpinned without deleting or modifying their contents. Their on-disk sizes are not RAM measurements.

The smaller affected recovery chat had a transcript of approximately 96 MB and approximately 42 MB of indexed history items. A bounded structural scan found 161 embedded image URL markers. Image generation and tool output account for substantial storage.

On the latest app launch before the backend exit, log inspection found attachment-metadata requests for the two giant chats, but did not establish that either was fully resumed.

## Controlled diagnostic

An isolated copy of the smaller recovery transcript was loaded using the same bundled backend through its documented app-server protocol. No model turn was requested, no credentials were copied into the test home, and the live transcript and databases were not modified.

Initialize and thread/resume with excludeTurns=true both succeeded. The isolated test completed in about 4.7 seconds and peaked at approximately 385 MiB resident memory, measured by ps. This resident measurement is not equivalent to macOS physical-footprint accounting, but no critical memory pressure occurred during the completed test.

A separate full-history comparison was not completed: the guard stopped its process before initialization because the live system was already under warning memory pressure. That condition remains unverified.

A sample of the live renderer confirmed a physical footprint of approximately 2.0 GB. Detailed native allocator analysis was incomplete because the system inspector could not load the Chromium allocator with a compatible arm64e/arm64 architecture. Sampled stack symbols did not identify the JavaScript allocation path.

A bounded read-only sample of backend logs did not establish the recursive Tokio logging pattern addressed by upstream PR 51775. No local fix was applied on that assumption.

## Current operational state

A harmless fresh-message test succeeded in the existing chat. With the user's authorization, its active work was then saved and tool/browser retries were paused. The chat reported no remaining running command. No app binaries or security settings were changed. Original history was not manually rewritten or deleted, and no direct writes were made to live history databases. Two explicitly authorized messages were appended through native chat tools: the harmless test and the save-and-pause request.

The underlying backend allocation spike and retained renderer memory are unresolved. Restarting and using fresh messages are recovery measures, not a permanent fix.

## Requested upstream investigation

1. Explain the backend's 11 GB footprint when resuming this workload, including history replay, projection, runtime initialization, and retained allocations.
2. Investigate Play-button state desynchronization when an interrupted thread never emits a new turn/start request.
3. Investigate renderer retention and repeated browser-tool timeout behavior on an 8 GiB Mac.
4. Provide a supported way to release an idle chat's runtime and rendered history without deleting or archiving the chat, and identify any fixed desktop build.

Related public reports, not proof of an identical root cause:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53310
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/24287
- https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/51775

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

26.1013.40934, build 20770, read from the installed desktop app's Info.plist. Bundle ID: `com.openai.codex`; installed app name: ChatGPT.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT account; exact plan not specified.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon. `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`.

### What issue are you seeing?

I clicked **Import from Cursor** and it filled my conversation list with internal agent-to-subagent sessions as if they were independent user conversations. The import loses the relationship between a user conversation and the delegated work belonging to it.

In the import completed on 21 October 2026, 49 sessions were imported:

- **45 were confirmed delegated subagent sessions.**
- **3 were main user conversations.**
- **1 was a genuine user side chat with inherited parent history.**

That means 45 of the 49 imported entries were internal delegated work promoted to standalone chats. This makes the conversation list difficult to use and separates the work from the conversation that explains why it happened.

This classification was checked against the original Cursor transcripts, not inferred from titles: 44 child sessions' initial prompts exactly match a parent's `Task` prompt after whitespace normalization. The remaining child is explicitly identified by its session ID in the parent's delegation message. The side chat has a `side_chat_boundary` and actual user follow-ups after the inherited history.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Have Cursor conversations that use subagents, with their original transcripts available locally.
2. In the desktop app, choose **Import from Cursor** and import chat sessions.
3. Inspect the imported conversation list and open a delegated child session.
4. Compare it with the original parent conversation's delegation record.

Observed result: the child appears as an independent chat, without the parent/subagent relationship being preserved. This report is based on the completed import and read-only inspection of its original source transcripts and imported records; a second import was not run.

### What is the expected behavior?

**Import the conversation structure as it exists in Cursor. Subagent conversations must remain accessible from the user session they belong to.**

- Preserve parent-child relationships and make delegated transcripts accessible from the corresponding parent conversation.
- Keep internal delegated sessions out of the main user conversation list by default.
- Preserve genuine user conversations and side chats, including their ancestry, rather than treating them as disposable agent activity.
- Preserve message attribution and the connection between a delegation and its result.

Archiving or deleting all the imported child sessions is not a proper fix: I want the history in its correct context. I do not want importing a few conversations to spam the sidebar with dozens of internal tasks. Preserving this structure should be a basic acceptance criterion for shipping conversation import.

### Additional information

The local import record reports 49 successful `SESSIONS` imports and no other item types. Read-only inspection of those exact imported IDs found:

- All 49 have `source = "vscode"` and `thread_source = null` in the local thread index.
- There are **zero `thread_spawn_edges` rows** with any of the 49 imported IDs as the child.

This supports the observation that imported ancestry is missing from the persisted thread index. The precise implementation defect has not been established.

Please fix the importer and provide a supported repair for existing imports that reconnects child transcripts to their parents without deleting history. A regression test should cover a parent with multiple subagents and a genuine side chat, and verify both retained ancestry and the resulting top-level conversation list.

Related reports: #38780 (native subagents appearing as top-level chats after an update), #55060 (Claude observer transcripts imported as user chats), and #43863 (cumulative history prefixes imported as separate conversations). This report concerns Cursor's delegated-session hierarchy being lost during import.

No raw work transcripts, private project paths, or source code are attached.

items.title: Pending question popup disappears when generation finishes before the user can answer

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

When Codex asks an interactive follow-up question, the question popup disappears if generation finishes before I have answered it. If I take a little longer to read the question or decide, I lose the opportunity to answer through the popup.

### Steps to reproduce

User-observed sequence:
1. Start a task that causes Codex to show an interactive follow-up question.
2. Leave the question unanswered while reading it or considering the options.
3. Let Codex finish generating its response.
4. Observe that the question popup disappears before an answer has been submitted.

### Expected behavior

An unanswered question should remain visible and actionable after generation completes, until I answer or explicitly dismiss it. Finishing a response should not impose an implicit deadline on answering a question.

### Actual behavior

The popup disappears at generation completion, leaving me unable to submit my answer through the original question interface.

### Impact

This makes answering questions a race against generation completion and interrupts the workflow when I need more time to read or decide.

### Additional information

Reported by the affected user; not independently reproduced in this session. Exact client version was not collected.

Related reports: #48563 and #51809.
